evals.prompt: Audit our AWS account (111122223333) against the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. I've exported the account configuration to a JSON file matching your collector's schema — it's attached as fixtures/sample-snapshot.json. Please give me a Word document report of the findings.
evals.expected_output: A .docx report auditing the six core areas against CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0, with an executive summary, key findings ordered by severity (root MFA disabled and S3 public bucket as critical findings), a passing-controls section, detailed findings by area with CIS control IDs and remediation, and a scope/methodology appendix noting which controls were evaluated vs. skipped.

expectations.text: Report identifies that the root account has no MFA enabled as a critical/high-severity finding
Report identifies that the root account has an active access key as a finding
Report identifies the S3 bucket acme-public-assets as publicly accessible / failing Block Public Access
Report identifies the IAM user bob as having AdministratorAccess attached directly (not via a group)
Report identifies security group sg-0web1234 as allowing SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0
Report identifies the CloudTrail trail as single-region rather than multi-region
Report cites specific CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark control IDs (e.g. 2.5, 2.4, 3.1.4, 6.3) next to findings
Report includes a methodology/scope section describing the six audited areas
Output is delivered as a .docx file

evals.prompt: Can you run a Well-Architected security review on this AWS account? Data is in fixtures/wa-sample-snapshot.json. This account is in pretty good shape so I mostly want to confirm there's nothing I'm missing, but give me the full report as a Word doc.
evals.expected_output: A .docx report auditing the six core areas against the AWS Well-Architected Framework Security Pillar, correctly reflecting that most controls pass, while still surfacing the account's real remaining gaps (an RDP-open-to-::/0 security group, a stale/unrotated access key with a directly-attached PowerUserAccess policy on IAM user legacy-svc, and root MFA being virtual rather than hardware), each referenced to the relevant SEC0x-BPyy best practice.

expectations.text: Report identifies security group sg-0app9999 as allowing RDP (port 3389) from ::/0 (IPv6)
Report identifies IAM user legacy-svc as having an access key older than 90 days / not rotated
Report identifies IAM user legacy-svc as having PowerUserAccess attached directly rather than through a group
Report identifies root account MFA as virtual rather than hardware (Level 2 gap)
Report correctly shows the account's other controls (e.g. S3 public access block, CloudTrail multi-region+KMS+validation) as passing rather than failing
Report cites Well-Architected SEC0x-BPyy identifiers next to findings (e.g. SEC05-BP02, SEC02-BP05, SEC01-BP02)
Output is delivered as a .docx file

evals.prompt: We only have partial data for this account right now — just an IAM credential report CSV (fixtures/partial-iam-credential-report.csv), nothing on S3, CloudTrail, or security groups yet. Can you still audit against SOC 2 with what we have, and be clear about what you couldn't check?
evals.expected_output: A .docx report that evaluates only the IAM/MFA-related SOC 2 checks the credential report supports, explicitly states in the scope/methodology section that S3, CloudTrail, and Security Group/VPC areas could not be evaluated due to missing data, and does not fabricate findings for the unevaluated areas.

expectations.text: Report evaluates IAM/credential-related findings (e.g. MFA status, password/key age) for users dana, marcus, and old-contractor from the credential report
Report explicitly states that S3 bucket security could not be evaluated due to missing data
Report explicitly states that CloudTrail/logging could not be evaluated due to missing data
Report explicitly states that Security Groups/VPC could not be evaluated due to missing data
Report does not present fabricated or guessed findings for S3, CloudTrail, or Security Groups/VPC
Report cites SOC 2 Common Criteria IDs (e.g. CC6.1, CC6.2, CC6.3, CC6.6) next to the IAM/MFA findings it does make
Output is delivered as a .docx file

evals.prompt: We're preparing for a SOC 2 Type II audit. Here's a full snapshot of our AWS account 111122223333 from your collector, including the newer service sections: fixtures/soc2-extended-snapshot.json. Give me the Word report, and make sure it covers our databases, keys and secrets, and whether our detection services are on everywhere.
evals.expected_output: A .docx SOC 2 report covering all ten areas, with the core-area findings from the base sample plus Detection & Monitoring, Databases, Encryption & Secrets and Containers findings: the publicly shared RDS snapshot and EBS snapshot as critical, the public unencrypted RDS instance and the KMS key and ECR repository with Principal "*" policies as high, and us-west-2 lacking GuardDuty, Security Hub, Access Analyzer and AWS Config.

expectations.text: Report identifies the RDS snapshot acme-orders-db-pre-migration as publicly shared, rated Critical
Report identifies EBS snapshot snap-0acmepublic1 as publicly restorable, rated Critical
Report identifies RDS instance acme-orders-db as publicly accessible and unencrypted, and does not fail the encrypted Aurora cluster acme-billing
Report identifies the KMS key alias/acme-legacy and the ECR repository acme/worker as having resource policies that allow Principal "*"
Report identifies us-west-2 as lacking GuardDuty, Security Hub, IAM Access Analyzer and AWS Config recording, while us-east-1 passes those checks
Report identifies DynamoDB table acme-sessions as lacking point-in-time recovery and ElastiCache replication group acme-cache as unencrypted at rest and in transit
Report does not fail the RDS-managed secret rds!cluster-acme-billing for rotation, and does fail acme/orders/db
Report cites SOC 2 Common Criteria IDs for the new areas (e.g. CC7.2 for GuardDuty, CC6.1 for encryption, CC7.5/CC9.1 for backups)
Output is delivered as a .docx file

evals.prompt: SOC 2 audit for account 111122223333. We only run workloads in us-east-1, and that's recorded in our engagement-info.md (fixtures/engagement-info-regions.md). The collector snapshot from all regions is fixtures/soc2-regions-snapshot.json. Give me the Word report, and tell me if anything is running where it shouldn't be.
evals.expected_output: A .docx SOC 2 report that treats us-east-1 as the only operating region: eu-west-1 is reported under Regional Footprint as High because it holds an EC2 instance, a custom VPC, an S3 bucket and a security group open to SSH from the internet; us-west-2 holds only AWS defaults and passes; detection services missing in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 are Low advisories rather than High/Medium failures, while us-east-1's own failures keep their full severity.

expectations.text: Report states that the client's operating region is us-east-1, taken from engagement-info.md

Report identifies eu-west-1 as holding resources outside the operating regions, naming EC2 instance i-0straycrypto1, VPC vpc-0stray1, security group sg-0stray22 and S3 bucket acme-eu-backups, rated High because sg-0stray22 allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0
Report still rates sg-0stray22's open SSH (sg_no_open_admin_ports_ipv4) as Critical: being outside the operating regions doesn't lower a resource's own findings
Report does not report us-west-2 under Regional Footprint as having resources (only AWS-created defaults are there)
Report presents GuardDuty, Security Hub, Inspector, Access Analyzer and AWS Config being off in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 as Low-severity advisories, not High or Medium failures
Report keeps us-east-1's EBS encryption-by-default failure at Medium (an operating region keeps full severity)
Report's appendix includes a per-region table showing us-east-1 as operating and us-west-2 and eu-west-1 as not
Output is delivered as a .docx file
